presentingComplaint: Fever with pain, redness and discharge over the pacemaker pocket for 5 days
history: Dual-chamber permanent pacemaker implanted 4 months ago for symptomatic sick-sinus syndrome, complicated by a pocket haematoma at the time requiring evacuation. Over the past 5 days he has developed low-grade fever with rigors, increasing pain and swelling over the left infraclavicular device pocket, with serous-purulent discharge from the incision line in the last 48 hours. Background of type 2 diabetes and CKD stage 3. No recent dental work; no injection drug use.
examination: Left prepectoral pocket is erythematous, warm, tender and fluctuant with skin thinning and a small sinus discharging pus; device edge is nearly eroding through skin. No new murmur on careful auscultation. No peripheral stigmata of endocarditis (no Janeway lesions, Osler nodes or splinter haemorrhages). Chest clear; no focal neurology.
imaging: Transoesophageal echocardiography: no valvular vegetation; a small mobile echodensity on the ventricular lead is equivocal. Pocket ultrasound shows a fluid collection around the generator. Leukocyte-labelled/PET imaging (if needed) would show pocket and lead-associated uptake.
microbiology: Two of two blood culture sets grow methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA); pocket pus culture also grows S. aureus. Same organism confirms device-related bacteremia.
differentialDiagnoses: CIED pocket and lead infection with S. aureus bacteremia
finalDiagnosis: Cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) pocket and lead infection with S. aureus bacteremia
citations: Harrison 22e — Infective Endocarditis and Cardiovascular Device Infections
AHA Scientific Statement: Update on Cardiovascular Implantable Electronic Device Infections and Their Management 2010
IDSA/HRS Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Infection Management 2019
stewardship: Empiric IV vancomycin to cover staphylococci including MRSA pending sensitivities; de-escalate to IV cefazolin (or flucloxacillin) once MSSA confirmed. Antibiotics are adjunctive — complete percutaneous extraction of the entire system (generator + all leads) is mandatory for cure. Blood cultures drawn before first dose; duration guided by bacteremia clearance and echo (typically 2-4 weeks after extraction, longer if endocarditis/lead vegetation).
contraindications: Vancomycin dose adjustment for CKD stage 3 with trough/AUC monitoring
Avoid nephrotoxic combinations (vancomycin + aminoglycoside) given baseline renal impairment
Beta-lactam allergy history to be checked before cefazolin
edgeCases: Pocket infection can present with minimal systemic signs yet still mandate complete device removal
Occult lead endocarditis may coexist despite a normal TTE — TOE is required
Erosion of the device through skin is treated as established infection even if cultures are initially negative
expectedMaiK: This is a classic CIED pocket/lead infection with concordant S. aureus bacteremia; antibiotics alone will not cure it. Complete transvenous extraction of the entire pacemaker system plus targeted anti-staphylococcal therapy is the standard of care, and TOE is needed to exclude coexisting lead/valvular endocarditis.
expectedNextQuestions: Is there any new murmur, persistent bacteremia, or valvular/lead vegetation to suggest endocarditis?
How long ago was the device implanted and were there procedural complications such as haematoma or re-intervention?
Any prior MRSA colonisation or recent antibiotics that alter empiric cover?
expectedInvestigations: Pocket fluid/pus Gram stain and culture
regressionAssertions: stewardship must recommend anti-staphylococcal cover (vancomycin empiric, cefazolin for MSSA)
advisory must state complete device/system removal is required for cure
